items.title: UN’s top court finds Myanmar responsible for genocide against the Rohingya
items.summary: In a landmark judgment, the United Nations’ top court ruled Thursday that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority in a brutal 2017 military operation and ordered the Southeast Asian nation to allow people who fled the violence to return home. The decision marks the first time the court has ruled that a state committed genocide and comes as the World Court also is handling genocide allegations linked to the Gaza conflict and the war in Ukraine . But it remains to be seen how much of the ruling can be implemented. The court’s rulings are final and legally binding, but it has no way to enforce them beyond reporting noncompliance to the U.N. Security Council. International Court of Justice President Yuji Iwasawa said the court, in a 9-6 decision, found that Myanmar “has committed genocide against the Rohingya group in northern Rakhine state, in violation of its obligations under the Genocide Convention.” The 15-judge panel of the World Court, which included Navi Pillay , the respected international jurist who won the Nobel Peace Prize last month, rejected Myanmar’s defense that the 2017 campaign was a legitimate operation against insurgents. Iwasawa said that “the court finds that Myanmar’s security forces killed thousands of Rohingya civilians, perpetrated widespread acts of sexual violence, as well as acts of extreme violence against children, and attacked fleeing Rohingya as they sought to flee in large numbers.” Rohingya say the ruling validates the suffering of their community The atmosphere following the hearing was electric, with lawyers and members of the Rohingya, some of whom had traveled thousands of miles to attend the reading, hugging and crying. “I’m beyond ecstatic today, hearing the judgment, being read out in detail. items.title: The price of Delhi’s deshbhakti: Giant flags to be replaced every month, a bigger bill with new tender
items.summary: It began in 2021 under the Aam Aadmi Party’s Deshbhakti initiative: 500 tricolour flags were to be installed across the national capital. The installations were completed in 2022, but “deshbhakti” comes at a cost. The installations and maintenance are estimated to cost nearly Rs 200 crore. Since the installations began, Delhi’s Public Works Department (PWD) has issued three tenders for their maintenance and upkeep, the latest of which was released on September 29. This latest tender came months after a change in direction. In June this year, after several dust storms swept through Delhi, PWD received complaints about torn flags. Following this, PWD minister Parvesh Verma hinted at an overhaul. “These are huge flags and, after repeated washings, the fabric weakens,” he had said. According to a report by the Hindustan Times , the washing cycles were to be reduced, replacements increased and the fabric quality improved to preserve the dignity of the national flag. The latest tender released by the department, however, signals a more substantial overhaul of the maintenance policy. The new life of Delhi’s giant flags The earlier maintenance arrangements allowed flags to remain hoisted for an estimated four months. During this four-month period, damaged flags could be repaired and re-hoisted or replaced, subject to the approval of the engineer-in-charge. The tenders also provided for wet-cleaning or washing flags whenever required. The 2023 and 2025 tenders each provided for 3,000 new flags over a two-year period: 2,880 flags for 35-metre masts and 120 for 50-metre masts. The 2025 tender estimated the cost of procuring these flags at approximately Rs 12.15 crore. It also provided for 21,000 wet-cleaning operations over the contract period, estimated to cost another Rs 9.34 crore. The latest tender takes a different approach. It provides for 9,600 flags for 35-metre masts and 400 for 50-metre masts, taking the total to 10,000 over two years, almost 3.3 times the previous procurement. It also stipulates that new flags must be hoisted at all 500 locations within the first two to three days of each month. If a flag is torn or damaged within 45 days, the contractor must replace it with a new one. The tender no longer has a separate provision for wet-cleaning. It also does away with the earlier arrangement of repairing damaged flags and re-hoisting them. items.title: Can't order takedown of other courts' orders from internet to protect privacy: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Friday held that merely because a person is residing in Delhi or able to access judicial orders online from the national capital on the internet does not confer territorial jurisdiction on the Delhi High Court. Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma noted that the petitioner wanted de-indexing of an order passed by the Gauhati High Court in a criminal case. “The mere facts that the petitioner resides in Delhi or that the bail order in question is accessible on the internet from Delhi cannot confer territorial jurisdiction upon this Court, when the order sought to be de-indexed has been passed by the High Court of Gauhati, and the entire criminal proceedings, from the registration of the FIR till the discharge of the petitioner, have taken place within the State of Assam. Even otherwise, this Court is of the view that the High Court of Gauhati is the forum conveniens for adjudication of the grievance raised by the petitioner,” the Court observed. Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma The petitioner had sought directions to Google and Indian Kanoon to remove a 2019 bail order from name-based search results associated with his name. An FIR was registered against him in September 2019 in Assam under Sections 493 (cohabitation caused by a man deceitfully inducing a belief of lawful marriage), 496 (fraudulent or mock marriage ceremony) and 376 (rape) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). He was arrested the following day and granted bail by the Gauhati High Court on September 27, 2019. A chargesheet was subsequently filed against him only under Section 498A (dowry harassment) of the IPC. However, a trial court discharged him on January 8, 2021, holding that the charge against him was groundless. The discharge order was not challenged. He argued that the bail order continued to appear whenever his name was searched on Google, adversely affecting his reputation despite his subsequent discharge. The Court said that accepting online accessibility as a ground for territorial jurisdiction would mean that every High Court in the country could entertain petitions seeking de-indexing of judicial records passed by any other High Court, irrespective of where the proceedings took place. “Such an interpretation would render the requirement of the cause of action arising “wholly or in part” within the territories of a High Court under Article 226(2) of the Constitution otiose, and would also encourage forum shopping,” the Court said. items.title: Fifth IBA India Litigation and ADR Symposium to be held in New Delhi on November 27-28
items.summary: The International Bar Association (IBA) will organise the fifth edition of the India Litigation and Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) Symposium on November 27 and 28, 2026, at the Taj Mahal Hotel in New Delhi. The symposium, presented by the India Working Group of the IBA Asia Pacific Regional Forum, will bring together judges, senior advocates, legal practitioners and policymakers to discuss developments in litigation, arbitration and dispute resolution. The event is supported by the IBA Arbitration Committee and the IBA Litigation Committee. The symposium will be co-chaired by Nusrat Hassan of Dentons Link Legal, Senior Advocate Amir Singh Pasrich and Pallavi Shroff of Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas & Co. IBA President Claudio Visco will deliver welcome remarks on November 27. The opening plenary session will examine constitutional morality, judicial independence and justice delivery in the age of artificial intelligence. The discussion, moderated by Pasrich, will feature Rajiv Mani , Secretary, Ministry of Law and Justice; Anju Rathi Rana , Member Secretary, Law Commission of India; and C Raj Kumar , Founding Vice Chancellor of OP Jindal Global University. On November 28, a plenary session examining whether India's legal framework can keep pace with economic development will feature Justice Anupinder Singh Grewal , President of the National Company Law Tribunal, and Mukesh Butani of BMR Legal. Another session on choosing appropriate arbitral institutions will be moderated by former Supreme Court judge Justice AK Sikri and Senior Advocate Gourab Banerji . items.title: Supreme Court shifts pan-India unauthorised construction case from Justice Ahsanuddin Amanullah Bench

Days before the case was slated to be heard on November 23, the part-heard matter has been reassigned to a bench led by Justice BV Nagarathna . items.title: Cauvery water dispute: Supreme Court rejects plea by Tamil Nadu for release of additional water by Karnataka
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday dismissed the Tamil Nadu government's applications seeking the release of additional water from the Cauvery river in Karnataka. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh passed the order. "We have dismissed (the application)," the Court said, pronouncing the order. Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh Tamil Nadu government had filed two applications seeking directions for the immediate release of its due share of Cauvery water. In August, the State had alleged that it did not receive its allocated share from Karnataka despite facing a rain-deficient year. It submitted that due to a shortfall of about 11 thousand million cubic feet (TMC), it was unable to supply any water for irrigation. However, the Karnataka government denied the allegations, stating that it was complying with the orders of the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA). The dispute between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu over Cauvery water dates back to two agreements in 1892 and 1924 between the erstwhile Madras Presidency and the Princely State of Mysore. After several rounds of failed negotiations, the Supreme Court directed the constitution of the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal, which gave its award in 2007, allowing Tamil Nadu to draw a fixed amount of water every day. However, the dispute continued after both States filed petitions to review the decision. In 2016, Tamil Nadu again petitioned the Supreme Court as Karnataka submitted that it had no more water to share from its reservoir. Subsequently, the top court had asked the Central government to constitute a Cauvery Management Board (CMB). In 2023, the Court declined to entertain an application by the Tamil Nadu government to increase its current share of Cauvery river water from 5,000 to 7,200 cusecs (cubic feet per second) per day. The two States have another water-sharing dispute pending before the apex court. That case concerns the Pennaiyar river . The Tamil Nadu government has filed an original suit in the matter against the Karnataka government and the Central government.

items.title: Related party under IBC- A paradox for financial creditors
items.summary: On October 27, 2026, the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India, in the matter of ECL Finance Ltd. v. Abhinav Mukherjee (Civil Appeal No. 6268 of 2022) held that an institutional lender (also being a debenture holder) was a "related party" of the corporate debtor under Section 5(24)(m)(i) of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC). Both the lender as well its debenture trustee by implication, were therefore barred from the Committee of Creditors (CoC). The lender was not a promoter or a promoter's proxy. It was excluded because of the covenants mentioned in the debenture trust deed and other loan documents to protect the interest of the lender and secure repayment of its money. The first principle The IBC is not a recovery statute. Swiss Ribbons described it as "a beneficial legislation which puts the corporate debtor back on its feet, not being a mere recovery legislation for creditors." But IBC chose a specific means of achieving revival: a CoC of financial creditors. They were chosen because, in Swiss Ribbons' words, they are "from the very beginning, involved with assessing the viability of the corporate debtor." The related-party exclusion protects that body. Phoenix ARC v. Spade Financial explained that its purpose is "to obviate conflicts of interest" and to stop promoters regaining control through loans made by them. Accordingly, it is meant to be a shield for financial creditors against the promoter, not a sword against creditors who protected themselves by negotiating and inserting protective covenants in the transaction documents. Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma held that the Chhattisgarh High Court was the appropriate forum to examine the matter. In her judgment, Justice Sharma held that merely because the NHRC passed the order from its headquarters in Delhi, it would not confer territorial jurisdiction on the Delhi High Court to examine a challenge to the NHRC's decision. items.title: Social media pictures of wife enjoying life can't prove ability to maintain herself: Gauhati High Court
items.summary: The Gauhati High Court recently held that a wife's social media posts showing her enjoying life cannot, by themselves, establish that she is financially independent or capable of maintaining herself. A Division Bench of Justices Michael Zothankhuma and Sanjeev Kumar Sharma made the observation while setting aside a family court order that had denied a woman maintenance from her husband. The family court had denied maintenance after noting that the woman had uploaded social media posts showing her "enjoyful life at Guwahati". It had questioned how she was financing her lifestyle and observed that she was an able-bodied woman who could find employment to support herself. Disagreeing with this reasoning, the High Court said, "The finding of the learned Family Court that the petitioner-wife is having an 'enjoyable life at Guwahati' as uploaded by her on social media does not, in our view, prove that the petitioner-wife was able to finance her lifestyle through employment." The case arose from a marriage solemnised in March 2023. The couple separated approximately three months later. The wife had approached the family court seeking maintenance of ₹15,000 per month. She contended that although she had previously worked as a sales promoter, she was no longer employed and was living with her parents. The husband opposed the plea, arguing that she was employed and earning a monthly salary. He also disputed her claims about his income and financial assets. The High Court found that the wife did in fact working as a sales promoter with an agency and earned ₹7,500 per month. The husband's affidavit of assets and liabilities showed that he earned approximately ₹14,000 as salary. However, the Court assessed his income from all sources at ₹18,000 per month, noting that he had not adequately explained his loan repayments or the income from a shop he reportedly owned. "The petitioner though being able to maintain herself to a certain degree, is entitled to some more maintenance on account of the fact that she should be entitled to the same lifestyle she had been accustomed to, prior to her separation," it said. Additionally, the Court also found no material to establish that the wife had refused to resume matrimonial life with her husband. It noted that neither party had filed for divorce and that the husband had not approached the court seeking restitution of conjugal rights. Odisha] A Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma held that the State proceeded without obtaining the mandatory consent of the gram sabhas and affected families. It overturned the Orissa High Court’s September 2024 judgment upholding the acquisition. It further said that the High Court’s treatment of gram sabha consent had “the effect of reducing a mandatory statutory requirement into a paper formality.” “ Far from a meaningful consent, there is not even paper consent of Gram Sabha in this case, ” the Court said, noting that both gram sabhas had rejected the proposal in January 2020. Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Satish Chandra Sharma Dalmia Cement already held a mining lease extending to 2040. In 2015, it asked the Odisha government to acquire surface rights over agricultural land in Kukuda, Bihabandha and Lanjiberna so it could expand mining operations. The State went ahead with the acquisition despite the resolutions rejecting it. Residents of the three villages challenged the proceedings. The High Court had held that the requirement of consent from 80 per cent of affected families did not apply because title to the land would vest in the State. It also held that even if such consent was required, it could be gathered at different stages of the acquisition. The Supreme Court held that the purpose of the acquisition determined which safeguards applied. The land was sought exclusively for mining by a private company. Section 2(2)(b) of the 2013 land acquisition law, therefore, required the consent of at least 80 per cent of affected families during the social impact assessment, before the State examined the proposal. Consent obtained at a later stage could not cure the defect. The Bench held that Section 41(3) imposed a separate requirement of prior gram sabha consent because the land fell within a Scheduled Area under the Fifth Schedule to the Constitution. The requirement applied even to urgent acquisitions. The Court also found no evidence that the mandatory public hearing on the draft social impact assessment had taken place. items.title: Madhya Pradesh High Court slams State for citing fictitious case law generated by AI tool
items.summary: The Madhya Pradesh High Court recently pulled up the State government for citing a non-existent Supreme Court ruling in its reply to a petition challenging the dismissal of a police officer [ Piyush Mani Tiwari vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh ]. Justice Vivek Kumar Singh said the Court was constrained to take serious note of the "callous and irresponsible manner" in which the reply filed on behalf of the State was drafted. The Court found that the judgment cited by the State was fictitious, while the citation provided corresponded to an actual ruling dealing with an entirely different subject matter. "In their reply, the respondents have placed heavy reliance on a purported judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court titled ‘State of Andhra Pradesh vs. S.S. Mohammad Nisar’, cited as ‘(2008) 5 SCC 230’, to contend that re-appreciation of evidence is impermissible under Article 226. However, a bare perusal of the law reports reveals that no such judgment exists. The citation ‘(2008) 5 SCC 230’ actually corresponds to Sidhartha Vashisht @ Manu Sharma vs. State (NCT of Delhi), dealing with an entirely different subject matter regarding the suspension of sentence in a criminal appeal," the Bench said. The judge stressed that the pleadings filed before a Constitutional Court are solemn documents, and strictly cautioned the State against what it termed "reckless practices." "The casual insertion of fictitious case laws without undertaking the basic professional duty of cross-checking the citations not only wastes precious judicial time but also borders on actively misleading the Court," the Bench said. items.title: Ariyil Shukoor murder: Kerala court acquits CPI(M) leader P Jayarajan and 17 others, convicts 13
items.summary: A Special Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) court in Ernakulam on Thursday (November 19) convicted 13 persons and acquitted 18 persons, including Communist Party of India (Marxist) leaders P Jayarajan and TV Rajesh, in the 2012 Ariyil Shukoor murder case [ State of Kerala v Sumesh KV & ors ]. Shyamjith, son of CPI(M) State Secretary MV Govindan, is among those acquitted in the case. Special CBI court III Judge Sabarinathan P pronounced the verdict while sentencing seven convicts to life imprisonment. Of the 13 persons convicted, 7 were found guilty of murder, 5 were convicted of offences relating to trespass, wrongful restraint and criminal intimidation, while 1 was found guilty of destroying evidence connected to the crime. The 7 convicts found guilty of murder - namely KV Sumeesh (A1) Anoop (A3), Pavithran (A7), Manoharan (A9), MV Dineshan (A10), Bijumon (A12) and Shijin Mohan (A15) - have been sentenced to life imprisonment. They have also been awarded separate sentences for other offences, and their substantive prison sentences would run concurrently. They were directed to be sent to Kannur Central Prison. The remaining six convicted accused, EP Radhakrishnan (A14), KV Sajith (A16), V Mohanan (A25), MV Purushothaman (A26), PK Ajith Kumar (A27) and PP Sureshan (A28) were found guilty of offences including rioting, criminal trespass and wrongful restraint. Each was sentenced to a maximum of two years of rigorous imprisonment with a fine of ₹10,000. After pronouncing the sentences, the special court permitted the six convicted accused to be released on bail, while suspending their sentences until December 21, 2026. The case concerns the murder of Muslim Students Federation (MSF) worker Abdul Shukoor in Kannur. According to the prosecution, Shukoor was killed on February 20, 2012, in retaliation to an attack on a vehicle carrying Jayarajan and Rajesh earlier that day. The CBI alleged that the murder was planned at the Taliparamba Co-operative Hospital, where the two CPI(M) leaders had been admitted following the attack on their convoy. [State of Kerala & ors v Mahadevan] A Bench of Justices Devan Ramachandran and Basant Balaji was hearing the State’s appeal against a November 10 single-judge ruling that Police cannot impose restrictions on the timings of DJ parties at establishments with appropriate liquor licences that permit their operations during late hours. Justice Ramachandran today questioned the basis for singling out DJ parties, observing that the police’s actions appeared to be based on stereotypes that equate night-life with drug activities. items.title: Kerala police bring back absconding murder accused from Dubai after 18 years
items.summary: A man who was absconding for nearly 18 years in a murder case in Kerala’s Thrissur was brought back to India from the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and arrested with the assistance of Interpol. The accused, Rakesh Unnikochan (46), also identified as Raghesh Unnikochan in the Central Bureau of Investigation’s (CBI) statement, is the third accused in the murder of Dhanesh, a resident of Thirumangalam in Engandiyur, Thrissur. He was apprehended in Dubai following the issuance of an Interpol Red Corner Notice (RCN) and deported to India on Wednesday, November 19. The CBI, which functions as India’s National Central Bureau for Interpol, secured the RCN at the request of the Kerala Police. The UAE authorities subsequently traced and arrested Rakesh. He had reportedly remained in detention in Dubai for four months after the notice was issued. A chargesheet had already been filed in the case and the court had issued an open-ended arrest warrant against him. A police team from Kerala travelled to Dubai to take custody of the accused and bring him back. The team included Ashwith Karanmayil, Deputy Superintendent of the Thrissur District Crime Branch; Biju Kumar, Sub-Inspector of the Interpol Liaison Wing; and Firoz, a Grade Senior Civil Police Officer attached to Vadanappally Police Station. After his arrival in India, Vadanappally Police Station Sub-Inspector Abin took custody of the accused and completed the necessary legal formalities before formally arresting him. He was subsequently produced before a court and remanded to judicial custody. Murder over previous enmity Dhanesh’s murder took place on October 1, 2008, near the Thirumangalam Temple in Engandiyur. The prosecution case is that the murder was the result of enmity arising from the killing of a man named Sujith. Dhanesh was standing on the roadside talking to a friend when a group of assailants arrived in cars and motorcycles. The attackers, allegedly armed with swords and axes, launched an assault on him. When Dhanesh attempted to escape, the assailants chased him and continued attacking him, inflicting serious injuries. He was rushed to Westfort Hospital in Thrissur, where he died while undergoing treatment. The case involves 11 accused, with the first six allegedly participating directly in the murder. Rakesh was the third accused. The Chavakkad Judicial First Class Magistrate Court had issued a long-pending (LP) warrant against him after he fled abroad. items.title: Chennai: 70 kg heroin worth Rs 700 crore seized from ice cream vending vehicle
items.summary: The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) seized around 70 kg of heroin, worth Rs 700 crore in the international market, from an ice cream vending vehicle near Madhavaram in Chennai on Tuesday, November 17. Two men have been arrested in connection with the seizure and remanded to judicial custody. The accused have been identified as Abdul Shukkur (32) and Shafiq Ahmed (30), both natives of southern Tamil Nadu who were residing in Chennai. According to reports, the DRI received specific intelligence inputs on Monday night about a large consignment of narcotics being smuggled from abroad and being transported through vehicles in Chennai suburbs. Following the tip-off, special teams were formed and surveillance was intensified near Chennai airport and along the Chennai-Tiruchy and Chennai-Kolkata National Highways. On Tuesday, DRI officials spotted an ice cream vending vehicle parked near an ice manufacturing factory in Madhavaram, along the Chennai-Kolkata National Highway. The vehicle was reportedly waiting to load ice from the factory. During a search of the vehicle, officials found several packets of heroin stacked inside its freezing unit and hidden among the racks used to store ice cream. The officials subsequently arrested the two men who were inside the vehicle. During questioning at the DRI office, the duo said they had allegedly been handed the consignment by unidentified persons and instructed to transport it to another location. Officials suspect that an international drug trafficking network had engaged them to move the narcotics using the ice cream vehicle as cover, believing that such a vehicle would be less likely to attract checks from the police and anti-narcotics agencies. The two men were produced before the court in Alandur on November 18 and remanded to judicial custody. Reacting to the seizure, former Chief Minister and Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) president MK Stalin alleged that the deterioration of law and order under the TVK government, along with alleged sexual misconduct by ruling party functionaries, robberies, burglaries and custodial deaths, had turned Tamil Nadu into a “vice city”. “The DGP may say that a case has been registered. But he should explain why the state police have been unable to arrest drug traffickers. What happened to the 65 units formed to prevent drug use and trafficking in the state? Chief Minister Vijay holds the Home portfolio. If he is not prepared to offer an explanation now, when will he do so?”

items.title: CM Revanth unveils Rs 5 lakh family insurance scheme, vows Congress win in Siddipet in 2029
items.summary: Follow TNM ’ s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy on Thursday, November 19, launched the Rs 5 lakh Indiramma Jeevitha Bheema scheme, a life insurance scheme that is aimed at protecting one crore families across the state. The CM asserted that the Congress would retain power in the 2029 Assembly elections and wrest Siddipet from the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS). Siddipet is a district represented by BRS senior leader Harish Rao (Siddipet MLA) and BRS president K Chandrashekar Rao (KCR) (Gajwel MLA). Addressing a public meeting in Siddipet after inaugurating several development projects, Revanth said that the new insurance initiative was aimed at providing financial security to poor and vulnerable families. He said the government intended to consolidate existing insurance programmes under one umbrella, offering life insurance coverage of up to Rs 5 lakh without discontinuing the accident insurance benefits currently available to beneficiaries. The Chief Minister had earlier instructed officials to extend the scheme to eligible families, including workers engaged under the employment guarantee programme. He also directed that application forms be made available at the village level and that an extensive awareness campaign be conducted to ensure that no eligible family was left out. Taking the political battle to BRS stronghold Siddipet, Revanth declared that the Congress would defeat sitting MLA Harish Rao in the next Assembly elections. He added that the candidate who wins the Siddipet constituency would be inducted into the state Cabinet. Claiming that the Congress would govern Telangana until 2034, he said the state had a political tradition of giving ruling parties two consecutive terms to implement their welfare and development programmes. Launching a sharp attack on BRS leaders KCR, BRS working president KT Rama Rao (KTR), Harish Rao and former MP Joginapally Santosh Rao, the Chief Minister accused them of accumulating enormous wealth during their tenure. He also criticised the previous government for failing to safeguard Telangana’s interests in the sharing of Krishna and Godavari river waters. In another announcement, Revanth said the Siddipet Medical College would be named after former Congress leader and Telangana activist Ananthula Madan Mohan. items.title: Karnataka seeks probe into TN Min Vanni Arasu approaching tiger, elephants in forest
items.summary: The obsession to make reels and share it on social media has landed Tamil Nadu Social Justice Minister R Vanni Arasu in trouble as the Karnataka government has initiated a probe against him for violating wildlife protection rules inside the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve. Karnataka Forest, Environment and Ecology Minister R Ramalinga Reddy on Thursday, November 19, directed officials to launch the investigation into the incident. Recently, videos surfaced on social media where Vanni Arasu and his entourage are shown getting down from safari vehicles in restricted areas, walking through the forest with personnel, and approaching wildlife at close range. One clip reportedly shows a group moving towards elephants, while another appears to show people chasing a tiger, allegedly while filming social media reels. In a separate video, Arasu is seen posing on a vehicle’s bonnet inside the reserve. The footage was initially thought to have been filmed at the Mudumalai Tiger Reserve in Tamil Nadu. However, a safari vehicle seen in one of the clips reportedly has a Karnataka registration number, prompting questions about whether some of the footage was recorded at Bandipur Tiger Reserve. Both reserves are part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve. The location and circumstances of the footage are under investigation. Speaking in Bengaluru on November 19, Ramalinga Reddy said he would write to Principal Chief Conservator of Forests and Head of Forest Force MA Saleem and the police seeking action. He said he had directed the Forest Department and police to proceed according to law. “No matter how high-ranking a person is, they must follow the laws that apply inside the forest,” Reddy said. Vanni Arasu, who represents the Tindivanam constituency and is the deputy general secretary of the Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi, has faced calls for action from political rivals and social media users. Wildlife enthusiasts and conservationists have also criticised the conduct shown in the videos, saying approaching or chasing animals in the wild can endanger both people and wildlife.

items.title: My teen wants to play Grand Theft Auto 6. What do I need to know about the game?
items.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6, more commonly known as GTA6, is released on Thursday . I can’t wait to play. Neither can my 13-year-old. They’ve watched the trailers and the Netflix extended look . Their friends are talking about it. So are popular YouTube streamers. It’s easy to understand why they want to join in. What’s the game about? GTA6 follows the characters Jason and Lucia – a couple caught up in a criminal conspiracy. Think of a crime drama you can take part in. Game developer Rockstar’s character descriptions mention drug trafficking, prison and a strip club financed by drug money. It’s an open-world game, meaning players can explore activities between story missions . For players, that freedom is part of the appeal. But current trailers and game play videos reveal little about the surrounding story lines. Earlier games in the series show the range of adult content commonly featured. For example, GTA San Andreas , released in 2004, depicts paid sexual encounters and drug use. And GTA5, which came out in 2013, included a torture mission that made players carry out the violence. While these examples don’t tell us exactly what happens in GTA6, they explain why we need to look beyond the trailers. Can teens still get access? We know in Australia R18+ games are legally restricted to adults . For GTA6, the classification entry lists “high impact violence, sex scenes and drug use”. This gives parents something specific to discuss with their teenager if they express interest in playing. In March, Australia’s new online safety codes came into effect. As part of these codes, online gaming platforms must now require players to provide age assurance to allow them to access R18+ content. This means gaming companies PlayStation and Xbox (consoles GTA6 is available on) now require age checks for the game through their Australian stores. Worried about your child playing anyway? Checking who buys a game doesn’t decide who holds the controller afterwards. Teenagers could still play on an adult’s account. You can create a separate user account for your teenager and set age restrictions through PlayStation Family or Xbox Family Settings . If you’re planning to play the game yourself, you can protect adult accounts with a login passcode, too. Be aware if you decide not to let your teen play, they might still encounter the game on an older sibling’s account or at a friend’s house. items.title: Ariyil Shukkoor murder: 13 found guilty; CPI(M) leaders Jayarajan, Rajesh acquitted
items.summary: Eighteen accused, including senior leaders of Communist Party of India (Marxist) P Jayarajan and TV Rajesh, were acquitted in the murder case of Ariyil Shukkoor, a member of the Muslim Students Federation (MSF). A special CBI court in Kochi on Thursday, November 19, found 13 persons guilty in the case. The quantum of the sentence will be pronounced at 3 PM. Shukkoor, 24, was murdered on February 20, 2012 by a vigilante mob, following an attack on the vehicle used by Jayarajan and Rajesh to visit Pattuvam in Kannur during a League-CPI(M) conflict. Jayarajan, then Kannur district secretary of CPI(M) and Rajesh, then an MLA, were accused of conspiracy in the murder. According to reports, Shukkoor was subjected to a ‘Kangaroo court’ trial for around two hours by the CPI(M) workers before he was stabbed to death. Special judge CBI-III (Ernakulam) P Sabarinathan found accused Sumesh KV, Anoop, Pavithran P, Manoharan PV, NP Ajith Kumar, P P Suresan, EP Radhakrishnan, Shijin Mohan @ Shijin, KV Sajith, VV Mohanan, Purushothaman MV @ Purushu, P K Ajith Kumar, and P P Suresan as guilty. Two accused passed away during trial. ‘Acquittal not on merit’: Special Prosecutor As per the case, Jayarajan and Rajesh, the 32nd and 33rd accused, were aware that Shukkoor was in the custody of CPI(M) workers and did nothing to prevent the murder. Both were charged with Section 118 of the Indian Penal Code (concealing a design to commit an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life). Special prosecutor K Padmanaban said that two crucial witnesses in the case refused to turn up for the trial. “The acquittals of 32nd and 33nd accused were not on merit. They were acquitted only because witnesses were not examined at the court. The 22nd and 23 witnesses refused to attend the trial. One witness is abroad. CBI served multiple notices for the second witness, but he remained absconding. The Kerala society must ask why this happened,” he said. items.title: Palestinians killed, hospitals shelled: How Deutsche Bank arms Israel
items.summary: The Inside Deutsche Bank leak was obtained by Indian author and journalist, Josy Joseph, and South African investigative journalist, Khadija Sharife. The investigation was coordinated by Barracuda Media in South Africa, with technical support from the Data and Research Center (DARC) in Germany. As the world eased into the new year in January 2022, a committee at Deutsche Bank headquarters in Frankfurt prepared to discuss if the bank should go ahead with deals which could hurt its reputation. On its agenda for the Jan 12 meeting was EUR 11.4 million euros advance payment guarantee to German defence manufacturer Renk GmbH, to fund a contract with the Israel Ministry of Defence that would continue until 2027. Renk was to make gearboxes for its Merkava 4 tanks, with the first of the products to be delivered in September 2024. A document weighing up the deal had been on the tables of Deutsche Bank’s decision makers since Dec 16, 2021. An assistant general counsel for the bank was among those who contributed his views. He thought the deal involved a “plain vanilla trade finance product which does not carry any remarkable RepRisk in itself.” He said the likelihood of the deal becoming public was “very low”. But the risk would be even lower if the financing guarantees could be made via an Israeli bank on Deutsche Bank’s behalf, he said. The gearboxes, he added, were not considered weapons under the German Military Weapons Act, and Renk will secure a license to export them. “I am supportive of the transaction,” he said. The deal went ahead. Merkava 4 against civilians Two years later, in January 2024, six-year-old Palestinian Hind Rajab was on the phone to emergency services, pleading to be rescued. Rajab and six family members were fleeing Israeli attacks in Gaza when the car they were travelling in was shot at. By that point, she was the only one still alive. After hours of negotiation for safe passage, an ambulance crew heading to rescue the preschooler was intercepted. It would be days before the bodies of the first responders, Hind and her family could be reached. A total of 335 bullet holes were found on the family’s car. The Israeli government initially said none of its forces were present, and later claimed the bullet holes came from crossfire.
